newsitem.title: LEBANON: U.N. SAYS HIZBOLLAH HARASSES ITS TROOPS IN LEBANON.
newsitem.headline: U.N. SAYS HIZBOLLAH HARASSES ITS TROOPS IN LEBANON.

text.p: The U.N. peacekeeping force in Lebanon accused Hizbollah guerrillas on Friday of harassing its soldiers in south Lebanon and threatening Irish and Polish troops at gunpoint.

Gunmen of the pro-Iranian Shi'ite Moslem movement three times stopped soldiers of the U.N. Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) in the past two days, put guns to their heads and forced them to lie on the ground while they checked their identities, a UNIFIL statement said.

On Friday "two Irish battalion vehicles were stopped by seven armed Hizbollah men near Kafra. The Irish soldiers were disarmed, forced to lie on the ground and threatened. Some rifle shots were fired around them," the statement said.

On Thursday, two vehicles with seven Hizbollah gunmen stopped a UNIFIL vehicle with two Polish soldiers, put guns to their heads, forced them to lie on the ground, checked their identities and destroyed the vehicle's radio, it added.
In another incident on Thursday Hizbollah gunmen repeated the harassment against three Irish soldiers in Tibnine, it said.
A Hizbollah (Party of God) spokesman called the UNIFIL statement an exaggeration.

A UNIFIL spokesman said Hizbollah appeared concerned by the recent import by a Lebanese businessman of a dozen second-hand trucks he bought from the UNDOF peacekeeping force on the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights seized from Syria in 1967.
UNIFIL had explained that the trucks had nothing to do with Israel but Hizbollah feared they might have been used to infiltrate Israelis into south Lebanon, the spokesman said.
"In all incidents, Hizbollah men said they wanted to check if there were Israelis in the vehicles," the U.N. statement said.

The Hizbollah spokesman said: "The facts mentioned by the UNIFIL statement exaggerate the reality...What happened did not exceed precautionary measures taken by the resistance and inhabitants to protect the liberated areas and civilians from any Zionist infiltration attempt in UNIFIL vehicles."

"The responsibility of these measures falls upon the party that permitted, through its actions, the enemy to use UNIFIL vehicles to threaten the security of our people in the liberated areas," he added.
